title: Spacing
description: How space shows what belongs together.

questions.text: Which spacing roles does it need?

questions.description: One density for everything, or a second for dense views.
How big the steps between spaces are. Small steps on a 4px grid suit dense screens and shared forms; big, even steps suit reading and big moments.
The place where space does its most visible work.

use_cases.description: A space token's use case names where the space sits, what it does and which way it runs. Each scheme gives every space token one use case and a multiple of its base. A use case with no reach runs both along a line and between blocks.

options.description: Inside one component: between its parts or around its content.
Between components: the space that arranges them on a screen.
Between the parts of one thing: a gap.
The padding of a box around things: an inset.
Along one line: parts that sit side by side.
Between blocks: parts that stack into sections.

jobs.how: grouping what is near and separating what is far, as the eye reads proximity (Gestalt), so a gap between groups stays clearly larger than a gap inside one

jobs.job: give content room inside its box
jobs.how: keeping content off the edge of its box, so the content reads as part of that box, and by setting the size of the box with the content
setting the hit area a finger or a pointer must hit; WCAG measures the hit area, not the drawn box (2.5.8: 24px at AA; 2.5.5: 44px at AAA), and padding or a label can make it larger than the box

jobs.job: keep the eye on its row
jobs.how: making each row a band the eye follows across, and a hit target when the row is clickable (WCAG 2.5.8: 24px)
letting the box grow when people override text spacing (WCAG 1.4.12), so a label never clips; a fixed height breaks this

hints.do: Never write a spacing as a number: not p-6, not gap-1.5, not p-[10px]. Every spacing has a name. Between things and on the page, use a role: gap-tight, gap-default, gap-group, gap-section, p-container, px-control, px-cell. Inside a component of your own, use a step of the component spacing map: gap-map-x2, p-map-x6.
hints.why: A number looks right in one scheme and wrong in the next. A name follows the scheme, so the screen keeps its density in every scheme.

hints.when: When you space the inside of a component.
hints.do: The component spacing map is the steps components space by. Each step is 4px × its multiplier (x1, x2, x3, x4, x6, x8, x12) × the scheme's rhythm, rounded to a multiple of 4px, at most 64px. A compact scheme has rhythm 1 and a spacious one up to 2, so a dialog's padding (x6) is 24px in one and 48px in the other. The scheme decides which steps hold still: x1 and x2 are the fine spacing inside rows, so lists stay lists in a roomy scheme. The hairline is a fixed 2px nudge. Pick the step nearest the space you want.
hints.why: One unit keeps everything on one grid; the rhythm lets each scheme decide how roomy its components are.

hints.when: When one component looks too tight or too loose.
hints.do: Don't change the rhythm to fix one component. The rhythm is the whole scheme's density. Pick another step for that spacing instead, or ask for a new role if the same spacing repeats across components.
hints.why: A rhythm change moves every component in the scheme at once.
